title: Behavioral finance
audience: a college student in a finance, accounting or business degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Explain how heuristics, biases and emotions affect investors, how limits to arbitrage let mispricing persist, which market anomalies behavioral models explain, and how advisers and institutions can design choices and processes that reduce costly mistakes.
primary_reading: Meir Statman, Behavioral Finance: The Second Generation (CFA Institute Research Foundation, free PDF)

weeks.8: Market anomalies: momentum, value and bubbles

blocks.deliverable: Explain five choices with prospect theory.
Find the biases in three investor stories.
Measure a disposition effect in sample trades.
Week 7 midterm; explain one bubble with behavioral ideas.
Analyze a merger driven by overconfidence.
Design a default that improves saving.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Bias audit: study a real investment decision or market episode, identify the biases involved with evidence, explain the price effects with course models, and propose a process to reduce the errors, in a three-page paper.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
